title: Blue Hour
description: The twenty minutes after sunset, lying on your back on the kerb of a city street: a shaft of sky walled by two towers, a crane, brick and glass, every vertical running in to the zenith. Drag across and the evening runs: the skylight falls three and a half stops while the shaft deepens from pale peach-cyan to cobalt, darkest straight overhead, and the one sodium lamp at the bottom edge trips on its photocell and warms slowly from a dim pink strike to amber. The lamp is a real emitter cut from the HDR panorama, so its bloom and halation through the film come from its own radiance.
intent: Genre spec idea 10, Blue Hour (factory/reality/genre-spec.md section 4), after Todd Hido's dusk houses and CineStill 800T: glow that behaves like optics, as the one night-adjacent piece. Reference: https://www.toddhido.com/ and https://cinestillfilm.com/products/800tungsten-high-speed-color-film-135-36exp . ?t=0..1 holds the time (0 = sunset, 1 = twenty minutes on); ?still=1 skips the reveal.

photo.name: Grzegorz Wronkowski, Modern Evening Street (Poly Haven HDRI, CC0)

sources: HDRI: Modern Evening Street, Poly Haven, by Grzegorz Wronkowski, CC0. https://polyhaven.com/a/modern_evening_street (8k .hdr: https://dl.polyhaven.org/file/ph-assets/HDRIs/hdr/8k/modern_evening_street_8k.hdr). Rectilinear worm's-eye view, 94 deg across, the axis pitched 84 deg up at yaw 116 (between the two towers) with the frame slid 0.2 half-widths below it, so the zenith and every vertical's vanishing point sit inside the frame; rendered 2x supersampled and shipped at 1440x1800. Offline split: the sky matte (depth from Depth Anything V2 plus a two-colour luminance and chroma projection at the edges), the cloud texture as a log luminance ratio over the smooth sky, and the one emitter in frame (a sodium lamp head) cut out as radiance above its surround, its diffraction star painted out of both layers; ambient (lights off) as log2 radiance -10..+3 in 8 bits, emitters as log2 -9..+14.
